steps.body: A short setup to get this app ready. Nothing here is required; you can close it and come back later.

steps.title: Load example data?
steps.body: Example data fills the lists, detail pages and dashboards so you can see the app working straight away. Each card has its own Load button. Pick "None" on a production install.

store._note: Configuration exchange, not rows. A configuration set carries the registers, schemas, objects, views, flows, sources and mappings that make one way of working hold together. There is deliberately NO `installable` allowlist: a set exists to introduce schemas the instance does not have YET, so listing schemas this app already owns would refuse exactly the sets worth installing. The trust boundary for a bundle is its publisher, enforced by the engine's source allowlist and trusted-key check. ⚠️ An EMPTY `installable` means install NOTHING, not install anything — omitting the key and declaring an empty list are different things.

Nothing is invented here: the Traffic page is untouched and stays routable at /traffic, and only its menu entry moves, becoming a card. Themes is NOT carded — it is configuration for how a portal looks, not a reading of what happened, and ADR-097 keeps a domain of the work in the main nav.

pages.title: Traffic

config.description: What visitors looked at, who they were, where they came from and whether they did what the portal hoped. Pick a portal, a period and a segment at the top; the numbers come from the daily figures the aggregation job writes every fifteen minutes, and Export downloads exactly what the page shows.

pages._note: portal-traffic-analytics. The three stats-blocks this page used to carry counted portalSession, revoked portalSession and portalMessage rows: authenticated-session bookkeeping that said nothing about visitors (task 0.1). The six widgets here read portalTrafficDaily through the object API and say 'not measured' for a portal with measurement off instead of drawing a zero. portal-traffic-visitors-and-geo added the period selector (on the overview, read by every widget through the report store) and the Visitors widget. portal-traffic-outcomes added Goals, Funnels, Forms and Custom dimensions, the missing pages under Pages and the searches under Sources. portal-traffic-reporting added the segment selector and the Export button on the overview, the roll-up note, and the Script errors widget. The Export is a button on the overview widget rather than a manifest headerAction: nc-vue's dashboard header actions cannot read the portal, period and segment the page has selected, and a download of the wrong selection is worse than none. portal-traffic-experiments added Experiments, Heatmap and Session recordings; the last two say "off for this portal" unless the operator accepted the switch's warning. portal-traffic-kpi-cards moved the four headline numbers out of the overview into four TrafficKpi cards below it. They follow the overview's portal, period and segment and carry no picker of their own: the page has one period. The page selects the portal named in ?portal=, which is how a portal page's KPI cards link here. The cards follow the portaliq/PtVerkeer board: two columns from Pages and Sources down, with the missing pages and the site searches as cards of their own (content.part on TrafficPages and TrafficSources).

pages.title: Availability

config.description: How available each portal was over the last twelve full months, measured by the portal itself every five minutes, with every outage. For a service level review.

content.label: Longest outage
content.caption: in the last twelve full months

enumLabels.site-error: The portal answered with an error
enumLabels.timeout: The portal did not answer within five seconds
enumLabels.health-degraded: The portal answered, but its health check did not say ok

content.text: Every five minutes the portal opens its own public site, through this installation's web address, the way a visitor would. It counts as available when the site answers within five seconds and its health check says ok. An interval in which no check ran counts as down. The check runs inside the installation, so it does not see an outage of the network in front of it. The hosting party's own monitor stays the reference for that.

pages._note: operate-availability-report, as the portaliq/PtBeschikbaarheid board: the portal is a page filter (published portals, by slug) that every card reads through @page.portal; three KPI cards from the report's summary, the months and the outages as tables over the same AvailabilityController answer (admin-only), 'How we measure' as an info note, and Download in the header. Reached from the Reports hub's Availability card; not in the main navigation (ADR-114 Decision 3).

config._note: Security-token archetype: a portalSession is a bearer session minted for one portalAccount, so what matters when opening it is 'who does this belong to, what trust level, is it still valid'. The body leads with the session's own fields (audience, organisation, jti, trustLevel, issuedAt, expiresAt, revoked) in an 8-wide data card beside a 4-wide Related panel that resolves the accountRef FK back to the issuing portalAccount — the schema's only outbound object reference, now expressed as a canonical $ref+format:uuid property (ADR-062 rule 7) so the Related panel can resolve it to a display name instead of a raw uuid. No child object-list: nothing in this register points AT a portalSession. No files/calendar/contacts/talk leaves: a session is a pure auth-edge token, not content-bearing. No lifecycleActions: revoked is a one-way flag flipped by logout/admin action, not a modeled multi-state lifecycle. Audit history stays a sidebar tab. Detail in the v2 shape: the body is one tab strip (Overzicht first, Historie last) and the facts that sit beside it are the sideColumn. The tab children stay in `widgets` and out of `layout`, or the grid and the strip would each draw them once.

config._note: A portal's menus, pages and glossary live HERE rather than as their own top-level navigation entries: they are not free-standing collections, they are what one portal is made of, and a fleet-wide list of 'all pages' answers no question an editor actually has. They are `object-list` widgets filtered on `portal: @object.slug` — the token resolves against the portal being viewed. NOT `@objectId`: these children reference their portal by SLUG, not by object id, and a filter naming a property the rows do not carry matches nothing and says nothing (see PortalAccountDetail, where exactly that went unnoticed). Each filter was run against the API before being written here: 7 pages, 1 menu, 2 glossary terms for open-tilburg. portal-traffic-kpi-cards: four traffic KPI cards head the page (page views, sessions, visitors, engaged sessions), the same four numbers the Traffic page shows. Each is a PortalTrafficKpi around nc-vue's CnStatWidget with its own period picker; the picker opens on its `default`, 30 days, and the card sends the picked preset as `days` through the `@range.preset` token. A card opens the Traffic page with this portal selected. A portal with measurement off reads 'Not measured' and asks for nothing. portal-home-page sits DIRECTLY under the KPI row and above the portal's own fields, because it reports a configuration error and an error nobody scrolls to is not reported. It is the only widget on this page whose subject is a route rather than a record: a portal with no published page at `/` serves not-found at its own address, which no other widget here can show. Its placement, not its registration, is what puts it in front of an administrator, and tests/portal-home-page.spec.mjs asserts both. Detail in the v2 shape: the body is one tab strip (Overzicht first, Historie last) and the facts that sit beside it are the sideColumn. The tab children stay in `widgets` and out of `layout`, or the grid and the strip would each draw them once. The four summary cards (domain, theme, status, administrators) are the sideColumn beside every tab except Instellingen and Historie, and Measure traffic sits beside Instellingen, as the portaliq/PtPortal and PtPortalInstellingen boards draw them.

pages.title: Pages
pages._note: The `open-layout` row action is the list-side entry to the layout designer (`PageLayout`). `type: "open-page"` is the declarative form: CnIndexPage's action dispatcher pushes `{ name: target, params: { id: row.id } }`, so the action needs no handler and no route string of its own. Its counterpart is the `edit-layout` header action on PageDetail, and both exist because the designer used to be reachable only by typing `/pages/<id>/layout` into the address bar.

pages.title: Page
pages._note: A page's BODY is a widget grid, and this detail page cannot edit one — it renders the object's scalars, so `body.widgets` shows up as an array of grid integers in a textarea. `PageLayout` is the surface that edits it, and until the `edit-layout` header action below existed nothing in the UI linked there: the designer was reachable only by typing `/pages/<id>/layout` into the address bar. The action carries NO `params`: vue-router fills a named target's missing REQUIRED params from the current route (`pickParams(currentLocation.params, …)` in its matcher), and `:id` is the same param on both routes, so `PageLayout` resolves to `/pages/<this id>/layout` on its own. That is also why the library's `open-page` dispatch does not pass params.

config._note: portal-page-traffic: four traffic KPI cards (in the Verkeer tab, as the portaliq/PtPaginaVerkeer board draws them) (page views, sessions, visitors, engaged sessions) for this one page, then the page details, then Incoming and Outgoing traffic side by side. The cards are the portal page's PortalTrafficKpi with scope 'page': they read GET /api/traffic/page with the page's `portal` slug and `route`, each with its own period picker, and open the Traffic page with the portal selected. A page is matched to its traffic by its route within its portal; see openspec/changes/portal-page-traffic/proposal.md. Adding widgets replaces the default detail body, so the page details are a `data` widget here, as on PortalDetail. Detail in the v2 shape: the body is one tab strip (Overzicht first, Historie last) and the facts that sit beside it are the sideColumn. The tab children stay in `widgets` and out of `layout`, or the grid and the strip would each draw them once.

pages.title: Page layout
pages._note: A page body is a widget grid on the shared 12-column geometry, and no built-in page type edits one: the detail page renders the object as fields, which for body.widgets means an array of grid integers in a textarea. This custom page places, moves and resizes those widgets directly, and is what the floating editing control on the site links to.

A portal's media library (site-page-seo-history-and-media T06-T09). An editor creates an item here and uploads its file on the item's page (the sidebar's Files tab, OpenRegister's object files); the newest file is the one served, so uploading a new one replaces the image on every page using it. Pages refer to an item as media:<id>, picked in the page designer's Media dialog. Deleting an item a published page uses is refused by MediaWriteGuardListener, which names the pages.

An ordinary index over the named `flows` source (config.entitySource) rather than the deprecated `flows` page type, reading OpenRegister's one native flow store (ADR-065), scoped to this app by config.app.

content.text: Portaliq reports how its connections stand; integriq puts them in one overview beside those of other apps.
A connection the app does not register cannot be checked. Add new connections in integriq.

pages._note: adopt-connection-registry (hydra connection-registry D8, hydra#667, #673, #674 and #676). The rows are integriq's `app_connection` objects, synced from lib/Settings/connections.json; integriq works out each status. The app=portaliq preset is the IntegrationsMenu entry's `query` (ADR-097 decision 5), which the index page merges into the fetch as a bare filter key. `showAdd` is false because a row nothing declared has nothing to check (D9). Add integration leaves for integriq's overview through the openIntegriqConnections handler in src/customComponents.js, because a header action's `navigate` only pushes a route inside this app. The page follows the portaliq/PtIntegraties board: its title with a count line, Add integration as the primary header button, pills All, Works, Needs attention and Switched off over portaliq's own connections (each pill carries app=portaliq, so the page shows only them also when opened without the menu's query), and a side panel with the connections that need attention and two notes on integriq.

Yes or no questions that rule out the portal's product pages (public-faq-and-product-finder). Evaluated in the visitor's browser; no answer is kept.

Blocks of widgets that belong to one organisation and are placed on pages by id (site-shared-page-blocks). Only a published block is shown, and only on portals of its organisation. The `open-layout` action opens the page designer on the block.

steps.body: A short tour of the main screens. It takes under a minute, and you can close it at any point and pick it up again from the help menu.
Flows automate the repetitive parts of this app. They live behind the Settings button at the bottom of the menu. Have a look, though you do not have to build one now.
